name: Clearout AI
description: AI-powered household inventory and listing app. Users sign in, organize items into projects, upload photos that AI extracts into item details, get a comp-grounded price recommendation (eBay Browse API + rules-based pricing, not just an AI guess), and get copy-ready listings for Facebook Marketplace/eBay/Craigslist.
purpose: Dario's primary summer recruiting project. Full-stack engineering (frontend, backend, database, external AI/API integrations) + Product Management (user research, MVP definition, metrics tracking). Learning goal: deep understanding of every line of code and product thinking.
status: Building the real product (auth, projects, upload, pricing engine, marketplace linking) after dropping the original waitlist-first plan on 2026-07-12. See .claude/plans/ for the current milestone.
instructionsForClaude: Dario is learning full-stack engineering + product management. For EVERY code or decision: (1) Explain what/why, (2) Walk through line by line, (3) Show design tradeoffs, (4) Ask if he understands. Learning is the goal — he should understand every decision. Also think like a PM: What problem does this solve? Who wants it? How do we measure success?

techStack.frontend: Next.js 16 (App Router), React 19, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS 4
techStack.backend: Next.js API Routes + Server Actions, Node.js
techStack.database: Supabase PostgreSQL with Row Level Security (RLS)
techStack.storage: Supabase Storage for item photos (private bucket, per-user path scoping)
techStack.ai: Google Gemini Vision API (item extraction), eBay Browse API (price comps)
techStack.auth: Supabase Auth, email/password only for v1 (Google OAuth deferred)
techStack.forms: plain useState for simple forms; React Hook Form once forms get more complex

keyArchitectureDecisions: Synchronous extraction/pricing in v1, not a polling job queue: API routes call Gemini/eBay directly and return in the same response; jobs table kept for status/retry tracking without needing real worker infra
Row Level Security (RLS): Each user can only see their own data at database level
Zod validation: All AI outputs and user inputs validated against schemas
Projects are schema-first from day one (items.project_id is not null) with a lightweight default-project-on-signup UI, since adding the FK later would mean a real migration

Pricing is a rules-based engine over eBay Browse API active-listing comps, not a single AI guess — Facebook Marketplace and Craigslist have no usable API for this, and eBay sold-comp data requires a restricted partner application
Marketplace posting is copy-to-clipboard + deep link for all three platforms, not auto-posting — none offer a no-approval API for individual sellers

gitWorkflow.mainBranch: main - always deployable, merges via PR only
gitWorkflow.commitStyle: Conventional commits (feat:, fix:, test:, docs:, chore:). No AI/Claude attribution. No em dashes.

productMetrics: Items uploaded and priced (real usage, not signups)
Items actually listed on a real marketplace using the generated copy
Pricing confidence distribution (high/medium/low) across real items
Time per item (minutes from upload to copy-ready listing)
Qualitative: does the recommended price feel directionally right
